records.title: Dispatch Loom
records.subtitle: Dispatch reconciliation tool
records.summary: Internal dispatch-desk tool for reconciling records: operators compared an overnight spreadsheet with the daily export, and the tool surfaced understandable exceptions, including visible warnings for late source files and visible empty rows. Ada personally built the Python parser and SQL checks, gathered requirements, explained validation failures, and was responsible for those components. Operators and supervisors used the tool; supervisors made final dispatch decisions. It was not a route-optimization tool or an externally sold product.

decisions.reason: The name, role, profile summary, and all listed denials are supported by the source.

The employer, title, dates, Dispatch Loom work, parser/check contribution, training, and qualification that the time reduction was a team result are supported. The linked tools and achievements are also consistent with the source.

The record overstates preferences and requirements as implemented tool behavior: the source says supervisors wanted understandable exceptions and operators preferred a visible warning for late files, but does not establish that the tool surfaced those exceptions or implemented the warning. The other
The source identifies Roster Note as a separate SQL handover checklist built at Harbor Tools and says Ada documented its night-shift handover; it claims no measured impact.

The six-run reconciliation-time result, 3-hour weekly difference, team attribution, Ada’s parser-and-checks contribution, coworkers’ changed habits, and the correction that delivery speed was not measured are supported.

The training, two workshops, handbook, and five worked examples are supported. The summary accurately preserves the unresolved count discrepancy between Ada’s recollection of 12 and the attendance sheet’s 14.
The source supports SQL checks for Dispatch Loom, the separate SQL Roster Note checklist, extensive SQL use, and the Data tools category.
The source says PostgreSQL was used for the production database, in the Dispatch Loom context, and lists PostgreSQL in the Data tools category.
The source supports using Git for version control on the Dispatch Loom work and lists Git in the Collaboration category.
The source supports training dispatch coworkers and explaining the workflow to a supervisor using an example; the Collaboration category is also explicitly supported.
The source supports personally writing the Python parser and lists Python in the Data tools category.

The source supports Docker exposure as a one-off exercise, and the summary clearly qualifies that exposure. However, the record is categorized as a skill, while a one-off exercise alone does not establish Docker competence.
